problem: Let (a_n) be a real sequence converging to L. Prove directly from the definition of convergence that (a_1 + ⋯ + a_n)/n converges to L.
Suppose a_1 ≥ a_2 ≥ ⋯ ≥ 0 and Σ_{n=1}^∞ a_n converges. Prove that n a_n tends to zero. Construct a nonnegative summable sequence for which this conclusion fails when monotonicity is dropped.
Let f:[0,∞)→ℝ be continuous and suppose lim_{x→∞} f(x) exists and is finite. Prove that f is uniformly continuous on [0,∞).
For n≥1 define f_n(x)=x/(1+n x²) on ℝ. Prove that f_n converges uniformly to zero, and determine the exact value of sup_{x∈ℝ}|f_n(x)|.
Let K_1 ⊇ K_2 ⊇ ⋯ be nonempty compact subsets of ℝ. Prove that their intersection is nonempty. Then construct nested, nonempty closed subsets of ℝ with empty intersection.
Let f:ℝ→ℝ satisfy |f(x)−f(2)|≤3|x−2|^(3/2) whenever |x−2|<1. Prove that f is differentiable at 2 and determine f′(2).
For every continuous f:[0,1]→ℝ prove that lim_{n→∞} (n+1)∫₀¹ x^n f(x) dx = f(1).

Let f_n:[0,1]→ℝ be functions and f:[0,1]→ℝ continuous. Suppose f_n(x_n)→f(x) whenever a sequence x_n in [0,1] converges to x. Prove that f_n→f uniformly. Give an example showing the implication can fail on ℝ even with all f_n continuous.

Suppose f is differentiable on (0,1), with finite limits lim_{x↓0} f(x)/x = a and lim_{x↑1} f(x)/(x−1) = b. Prove that for each c strictly between a and b there exists t∈(0,1) with f′(t)=c. Do not assume f′ is continuous.

Construct a bounded, nonnegative Riemann integrable f on [0,1] whose zero set is dense and whose supremum equals 1. Prove in addition that every bounded, nonnegative Riemann integrable function on [0,1] with dense zero set has integral zero.
